Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement
Topic 3.3: Capacity (how much a container can hold)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capacity (how much a container can hold), part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: how many How many small containers can fill the big container?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Capacity (how much a container can hold) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learners find out how many small containers can fill a big one.

Values:
Responsibility: learners fill and empty containers without spilling over water or sand. They also team up to accomplish filling

and emptying activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Hygiene: learners observe hygiene as they do filling and emptying activities (not to drink dirty water).

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able relate water and sand concepts to similar concepts in natural resources in Environmental Activities.
